title: A Protocol for the Static
premise: August Vasquez smuggles memories—recorded human experience—past orbital customs for the forgotten colony of Meridian's Rest, whose slow suffocation under a corporate quarantine nobody reports. When he finds his own dead sister's name on the manifest of the Halcyon, a ship that never flew, he learns the quarantine was engineered to erase the colony from record, and that her memory-recording is the only proof. Racing a purge signal to the edge-of-dead-space relay, August must choose between broadcasting the truth and preserving the last intact recording of his sister, and in the end he splices them together: her voice becomes the evidence, transmitted as the relay burns behind him.
about_author: Gideon Brightwater spent nine years as a freight manifest clerk on a decommissioned orbital platform before turning to fiction, a job he credits for his obsession with paperwork as horror. He writes slow-burn science fiction about people history decided not to keep.

chapters.title: Contraband in the Corpus Callosum
chapters.summary: August runs a shipment of black-market memories through Meridian Orbital Customs, hiding grief-recordings inside shipping telemetry. POV: August. Establishes his craft, his cynicism, and the colony's quiet decay below. Emotional beat: weary competence masking dread.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Auditing old cargo logs, August finds the Halcyon—a ship never launched—with his sister Ilsa Vasquez listed among its passengers, dated three years after her death. POV: August. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past refuses to stay buried.

chapters.title: Meridian's Rest, Population Declining
chapters.summary: August descends to the surface colony to trace the name, walking streets where power rationing has gone from inconvenience to lethality. He interviews an old dockworker who remembers Ilsa boarding something. POV: August. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: Customs Chief Okafor
chapters.summary: Customs chief Adaeze Okafor summons August, aware of his smuggling but offering immunity if he investigates the Halcyon anomaly quietly. Her motives are opaque. POV: August. Emotional beat: the hunter wearing the mask of an ally.

chapters.title: What Memory Weighs
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young August and Ilsa recording each other's childhoods on salvaged rigs, inventing the rituals that became his trade. POV: alternating past-tense Ilsa fragments embedded in August's recollection. Emotional beat: tenderness as origin story.

chapters.title: The Quarantine Nobody Filed
chapters.summary: August discovers the colony's 'medical quarantine' has no originating document—it exists only as enforcement, a hole in the bureaucracy shaped like ten thousand lives. POV: August, with a brief Okafor interlude. Emotional beat: cold horror of administrative erasure.

chapters.title: Passengers of a Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing missing persons, August finds forty-one names on the Halcyon manifest—all colonists who died during the first quarantine year. Someone recorded their deaths as departures. POV: August. Emotional beat: mourning weaponized.

chapters.title: Okafor's Bargain Tightens
chapters.summary: Okafor reveals she suspects Halcyon Corp itself authored the erasure, but warns August that helping him will cost her career—or worse. She gives him a customs override key. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: loyalty offered at a price neither can count yet.

chapters.title: Signal From Dead Space
chapters.summary: A repeating transmission begins emanating from the edge-of-dead-space relay: a fragment of Ilsa's voice, looping. The purge signal that will wipe all colonial records is scheduled to arrive in nineteen days. POV: August. Emotional beat: hope arriving as an alarm clock.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Network Frays
chapters.summary: August calls in favors from fellow smugglers to reach the relay; two refuse, one informs on him, and the port locks down. He realizes someone inside the network sold the route. POV: August with smuggler Renn's perspective briefly. Emotional beat: betrayal in a community built on discretion.

chapters.title: Flight Plan: Nowhere Legal
chapters.summary: August steals a derelict hauler, the Long Answer, and plots an illegal burn toward dead space with Okafor's override key spoofing his transponder. POV: August. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of finally choosing a side.

chapters.title: Pursuit Vector
chapters.summary: Halcyon Corp security vessel Vantage picks up the spoof and pursues. A cat-and-mouse sequence through debris fields; August jettisons legitimate cargo to gain delta-v. POV: alternating August and Vantage captain Sorel. Emotional beat: the machinery of erasure has a face now.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Recording, Part One
chapters.summary: Trapped in transit, August plays the recovered fragment: Ilsa's deathbed testimony describing how Halcyon seeded the quarantine and staged the Halcyon's passenger list. POV: Ilsa via recording, framed by August. Emotional beat: intimacy with the dead as evidence.

chapters.title: Sorel's Doubt
chapters.summary: Captain Sorel, ordered to destroy rather than detain, requests verification and receives a falsified directive—her first crack of doubt. She closes distance anyway. POV: Sorel. Emotional beat: complicity examined.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge of Everything
chapters.summary: August reaches the ancient relay station, decaying and half-powered, and finds it already occupied: a squatter technician, Wren, who has been maintaining the loop of Ilsa's signal for years without knowing its source. POV: August. Emotional beat: unexpected kinship in a dead place.

chapters.title: Wren's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren admits she intercepted the original broadcast and has been too afraid to forward it—forwarding means the corporation learns the relay still works. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: cowardice and conscience wrestling in one small body.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days Become Four
chapters.summary: The purge signal arrives early; the Vantage enters weapons range. August, Wren, and the failing relay have hours, not days, to splice Ilsa's full testimony with corroborating manifests and aim it at every open channel. POV: August. Emotional beat: time collapsing around a decision.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth
chapters.summary: August confronts the choice: transmitting Ilsa's recording will overwrite and corrupt it—the only intact copy of her voice will be consumed by the broadcast. Keeping it means the colony stays erased forever. POV: August, alone. Emotional beat: the book's thematic heart laid bare.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: August splices her testimony into the transmission and sends it wideband as the Vantage fires. The relay takes damage; Sorel, receiving the truth mid-burn, hesitates—and her hesitation lets the signal escape. POV: alternating August and Sorel. Emotional beat: climax; sacrifice made audible.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Voice
chapters.summary: The relay goes dark. August drifts in the wrecked station with Wren, holding nothing of his sister but the memory of sending her. Sorel, mutinying quietly, does not report survivors. POV: August. Emotional beat: hollow, clean grief.

chapters.title: Meridian's Rest, Population Counted
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the broadcast forces an inquiry; aid ships arrive at the colony, and names return to official records—including forty-one passengers of the Halcyon, reclassified as deceased. Okafor testifies. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: justice as paperwork, finally honest.

chapters.title: A Protocol for the Static
chapters.summary: August returns to smuggling, but now records the colony deliberately—an archive disguised as contraband, so no one can be erased again. In the static between channels he sometimes thinks he hears Ilsa laughing. POV: August. Emotional beat: inheritance accepted; memory chosen over safety.
